title: Welcome promises 'no cloud' and 'nothing leaves' while her engine is a cloud model
body:
## Summary
The first-launch screen tells the person 'It all runs on this machine. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.' and 'Nothing leaves it unless you say so.', while every turn she takes is a model call to a hosted engine.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/companion/welcome.tsx:387 says of the page 'Nothing leaves it unless you say so.' and apps/desktop/src/companion/welcome.tsx:399 says 'It all runs on this machine. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.' The same window's Record lists 'Model calls' with a model name and a dollar cost per call (apps/desktop/src/companion/pages.tsx:129-151, rows from model.ts with cost_usd), and the engine line on this very screen probes for a CLI engine (Claude/Codex) that sends the page text she reads to a hosted model. The daemon and the record are local; the reasoning is not. This is a claim about where the person's data goes (public-claim-provenance: a claim on a surface must be true of the product). What 'fixed' means is a product decision: say plainly that the page text she reads goes to the engine the person chose, or scope the claim to what is true (no Athena account, no Athena telemetry).

## Flow
- First launch shows the Welcome form
- The person reads 'No account, no cloud, no telemetry' and 'Nothing leaves it unless you say so'
- Their first turn sends the page text she read to the hosted engine; the Record then shows the model call and its cost

## Expected impact
Every first-time user reads it; a privacy-sensitive user would decide on it. Changing it changes the product's promise, so the owner words it. Could break: nothing technical; tests pinning the welcome copy (views tests) would need the new sentence.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the welcome claim matches where data goes
Before: 2 sentences on the welcome screen claim no data leaves and no cloud is used; the Record shows hosted model calls with cost
After: unmeasurable - the right sentence is the owner's wording
Method: simulation - walked the welcome copy against pages.tsx's Model calls section and the engine probe; no gate can decide a product promise
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Her depth pages are announced as 'Record' and 'Origins', twice each
body:
## Summary
pages.tsx labels the Record and apps levels 'Record' and 'Origins' (developer words) and gives both the section and its scrolling region that same name, so a screen reader announces two landmarks per page, one of them jargon.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/companion/pages.tsx:219 and :222 pass label='Record' / label='Origins' to Level, which puts it on the section (apps/desktop/src/companion/pages.tsx:22 aria-label={label}) and again on the inner role=region (apps/desktop/src/companion/pages.tsx:31). The visible heading and crumb say 'The record' and 'The apps she may act on'; 'Origins' appears nowhere a sighted person reads. Fixed: the label is the visible heading, and the inner scroller is named by the section (aria-labelledby or no second label). The pins live in apps/desktop/src/companion/views.test.tsx:433-434 (desktop-companion-pane's test), which is why this round did not build it.

## Flow
- Open the ledger, press the record icon
- A screen reader lands on region 'Record' inside region 'Record'
- The apps icon gives region 'Origins' inside region 'Origins'

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users hear the page's own words once. Could break: views.test.tsx's two label pins, updated in the same change.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each depth page announced once, in the words on screen
Before: 2 landmarks per page, labels 'Record'/'Origins' (jargon), pinned at views.test.tsx:433-434
After: 1 landmark per page labelled 'The record' / 'The apps she may act on' (predicted)
Method: simulation - read pages.tsx and the pins; the build needs the pane context's test file
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: translate.test.ts: translate(`tabs.read → not read: <each tabReadRefusal detail>`) has no snake_case token in title or sub; seeded red on today's 'tabs_read' / 'page_read'
title: A refused tab read tells the person 'read it with page_read'
body:
## Summary
The tab-read refusals the run store writes into her rail name internal tools: 'Tabs_read needs the url of an open tab' and 'that is the tab this turn is on; read it with page_read'.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:337 detail 'tabs_read needs the url of an open tab' and apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:340 'that is the tab this turn is on; read it with page_read' are pushed as `<tool> → not read: <detail>` (apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1220); the translator capitalises the reason and shows it as the step's sub ('Tabs_read needs the url of an open tab. Nothing was changed.'). The same detail is also the model's error, where the tool names are useful, so the fix is two strings (one for her, one for the model) in stores/run.ts, outside this context.

## Flow
- She calls tabs.read without a url, or on the tab she is on
- run.ts refuses and pushes the detail
- Her rail reads 'Did not read the tab' over 'Tabs_read needs the url...' / '...read it with page_read'

## Expected impact
The person stops seeing tool identifiers; the model keeps its precise error. Could break: tests pinning the refusal detail in stores/run.test.ts.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no internal tool name in a sentence the person reads
Before: 2 of 4 tabReadRefusal details carry a snake_case tool name into the rail
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - read run.ts:331-349 and walked the not-read path through translate(); the fix is in stores/run.ts (another context)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Code inside bold in her markdown prints its backticks
body: ## Summary rich.tsx draws `**bold**` and `` `code` `` but not one inside the other: '**run `doctor` now**' renders bold text with the backticks typed out. ## Description apps/desktop/src/companion/rich.tsx:16 MARKS matches the bold span first and apps/desktop/src/companion/rich.tsx:26 puts its inside into as one text node, so a code mark inside it is never read. The model does write a name in backticks inside the one bold line it uses for 'the thing to notice' (the file's own header, rich.tsx:5-7). Fixed: the inside of a bold span goes through the code split (text nodes only, as today - no HTML). ## Flow - She answers '**Run `athena doctor` first**' - RichMessage draws Run `athena doctor` first - The person sees the backticks ## Expected impact Her emphasis reads cleanly. Could break: nothing outside rich.tsx; plainOf already strips both marks. ## Evaluation Claim: user - marks never shown as typed Before: '**a `b`**' renders with 2 literal backticks After: 0 literal backticks (predicted) Method: probe - traced MARKS on the sample by hand; unbuilt for round budget Result: better Gate: none

instrument: jsdom slip test: press 'Read it first' -> document.activeElement is 'Back to the decision' and .sl-front is inert; press it -> focus returns to 'Read it first'; seeded red on today's lost focus
title: Flipping a decision card leaves keyboard focus on the face turned away
body:
## Summary
'Read it first' flips the slip but moves no focus: focus stays on a button of the front face, which is now turned away and pointer-events:none but still focusable, and 'Back to the decision' must be found by tabbing.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/companion/slip.tsx:321 setFlipped(card.id) only; the front Face (apps/desktop/src/companion/slip.tsx:304) has no inert/aria-hidden when `back` is true, while companion.css .sl-card.flipped .sl-front rotates it away. This round made the unflipped BACK inert (ebefefee); the mirror case (front while flipped) needs focus to move to the back's first control and return on 'Back to the decision', which is a focus-management change best measured in jsdom with real focus.

## Flow
- Tab to 'Read it first' and press Enter
- The card flips; focus is still on the hidden front button
- Tab walks the hidden front's controls (Approve, Decline, Later) before reaching the back

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users read the back without hunting. Could break: the A/D shortcuts must keep working while flipped (they are global).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus follows the face the person sees
Before: after flip, focus on a hidden control; hidden front controls remain in Tab order
After: focus on 'Back to the decision'; front inert while flipped (predicted)
Method: simulation - read slip.tsx and companion.css flip rules; needs a focus instrument
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The engine line's live region wraps its own buttons
body:
## Summary
welcome.tsx puts role='status' on the span that also holds 'Check again' / 'Use <engine>' buttons, so the live region re-announces button labels and the buttons sit inside a polite region.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/companion/welcome.tsx:343 <span role='status'> wraps the engine text and, when missing, the action span with buttons (apps/desktop/src/companion/welcome.tsx:346-361). 'Checking…' toggles inside it, so each probe re-reads the whole line including button names. Fixed: the status is the text only; the buttons sit beside it.

## Flow
- First launch with no engine found
- Press 'Check again'
- The live region announces the sentence plus 'Checking…' and 'Use Codex' button names

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users hear the engine state once per change. Could break: views tests that select the engine line's text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a live region announces state, not controls
Before: 1 live region containing up to 2 buttons
After: 0 buttons in the live region (predicted)
Method: simulation - read welcome.tsx; instrument named
Result: better
Gate: none
